description: mongo_fdw builds the mongodb:// connection URI by inserting option values without percent-encoding them, so URI metacharacters (@ : / ? # & =) in a value are parsed as part of the URI structure. A role that is not a superuser but has USAGE on a foreign server can set the username and password options in its own user mapping. An @ or other metacharacter in those values can point the connection at a host the attacker controls, allowing connection redirection, credential capture and man-in-the-middle attacks. Server-level options such as the address, database and replica set can be injected the same way. The issue is fixed in mongo_fdw 5.6.0. From mongo_fdw 5.6.0, mongo_fdw builds the URI with the libmongoc URI API, which encodes credentials, and rejects URI metacharacters in the other option values.
